metadata.author_perspective: Dual-degree genetics researcher — molecular genetics + computational genomics
metadata.review_standard: Every claim must trace to DOI. Preference: meta-analyses > RCTs > Phase 2 > preclinical > in vitro
critical_gaps_identified: Missing epigenetic reprogramming axis (Yamanaka/OSK partial reprogramming)
No inflammaging/NF-κB pathway — master driver of immunosenescence
No mitophagy axis — Urolithin A has Phase 3 data (UPLIFT)
Missing genetic context — FOXO3/APOE/CETP polymorphisms determine responder status
AKG Rejuvant paper (Demidenko 2021) has methodological concerns — noted
Taurine excluded despite massive 2023 Science dataset (Singh et al.)

genetic_stratification.description: Not all humans benefit equally from longevity interventions. Genetic variants determine pathway activity, enzyme levels, and drug metabolism. A rigorous platform MUST stratify by genotype.

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: G allele upregulates FOXO3 → increased autophagy, antioxidant genes, apoptosis of damaged cells
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: Individuals with TT genotype benefit MORE from rapamycin/metformin (compensates for low FOXO3 activity)
key_longevity_polymorphisms.evidence: Willcox et al., PNAS 2008 (DOI: 10.1073/pnas.0801030105); Flachsbart et al., Aging Cell 2009 (DOI: 10.1111/j.1474-9726.2009.00487.x)

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: ε4 → impaired cholesterol clearance, neuroinflammation, Aβ aggregation, reduced SIRT1 expression
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: ε4 carriers: PRIORITIZE NAD+ boosters (NMN/NR) — SIRT1 underexpressed. Also benefit from rapamycin (reduces Aβ via autophagy). AVOID telomerase activators (ε4 + telomerase = glioblastoma risk)
key_longevity_polymorphisms.evidence: Sebastiani et al., Aging 2019 (DOI: 10.18632/aging.101967); Schachter et al., Nat Genet 1994 (DOI: 10.1038/ng0194-29)

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: Larger HDL particles → reduced cardiovascular mortality. These individuals naturally have longevity pathway advantage
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: II genotype carriers benefit more from spermidine (cardioprotective) and metformin (vascular protection)

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: Gain-of-function mTOR variants → accelerated aging, poor autophagy
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: High-mTOR genotypes: respond better to rapamycin. Low-mTOR: already partially protected, lower dose needed

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: G allele → higher SIRT1 expression → better NAD+ utilization
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: AA genotype (low SIRT1): HIGHEST priority for NMN supplementation — enzyme is present but substrate-limited

key_longevity_polymorphisms.mechanism: C allele → higher telomerase expression in stem cells → slower telomere attrition
key_longevity_polymorphisms.implication_for_cocktail: AA genotype (short telomeres): may benefit from TA-65, BUT only if p53/RB pathway intact. Must check TP53 somatic mutations first.

additional_compounds_genetics_driven.name: Urolithin A
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.mechanism: Gut microbiome-derived metabolite of ellagitannins. Directly activates mitophagy via PINK1/Parkin — clears damaged mitochondria. Increases mitochondrial membrane potential, muscle endurance, NAD+ levels.
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.genetic_basis: Mitophagy capacity declines with age partly due to reduced PINK1 expression (PARK6 locus). Urolithin A bypasses genetic bottleneck by directly activating the pathway downstream.

clinical_evidence.key_result: 500mg/day for 4 months improved muscle strength by 12% in elderly. Increased plasma acylcarnitines (mitochondrial output). First mitophagy compound with Phase 3 data.

key_papers.title: Urolithin A induces mitophagy and prolongs lifespan in C. elegans and increases muscle function in rodents
Urolithin A supplementation for muscle health in older adults

dosing.bioavailability: Direct absorption (no microbiome conversion needed for synthetic form)

safety.known_risks: Well-tolerated. GRAS status. No SAEs in 4-month Phase 3.

quantum_sim_params.quantum_advantage_reason: PINK1 kinase activation involves conformational allosteric change — limited quantum advantage, classical sufficient

additional_compounds_genetics_driven.name: Taurine
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.mechanism: Essential for mitochondrial tRNA taurine modification (τm5U, τm5s2U). Without taurine modification, mitochondrial translation stalls → Complex I dysfunction → accelerated aging. Also: antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, bile acid conjugation.
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.genetic_basis: Taurine biosynthesis from cysteine requires CSAD enzyme. CSAD expression declines 60% with age (Singh et al. 2023). Blood taurine halves by age 60. This is a GENETIC PROGRAM of decline, not just dietary deficiency.

clinical_evidence.key_result: Massive cross-species study (Science 2023): taurine decline DRIVES aging. Supplementation extended healthspan 10-12% in mice (equivalent to ~7-8 human years). Reversed epigenetic age markers.

key_papers.title: Taurine deficiency as a driver of aging
Taurine and aging: implications for tissue homeostasis

dosing.human_dose: 1000-3000 mg/day oral (study used ~1g/kg in mice → ~6g/day human, but lower doses being tested)

safety.known_risks: Endogenous amino sulfonic acid. Used in energy drinks for decades. WHO ADI not established (considered safe). Concerns only at extreme doses (>10g/day).

quantum_sim_params.quantum_advantage_reason: No significant quantum advantage — classical methods adequate for taurine interactions

additional_compounds_genetics_driven.name: Sulforaphane (Nrf2 activator)
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.mechanism: Modifies cysteine residues on KEAP1 (Cys151, Cys273, Cys288) → releases Nrf2 from degradation → Nrf2 translocates to nucleus → activates 200+ cytoprotective genes (NQO1, HMOX1, GCLC, GPX). Master antioxidant AND anti-inflammatory switch.
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.genetic_basis: Nrf2 (NFE2L2) expression declines with age due to epigenetic silencing (increased KEAP1 promoter methylation). Sulforaphane directly bypasses this genetic decline by attacking the protein-level regulation.

clinical_evidence.key_result: Broccoli sprout extract (containing sulforaphane) reduced NF-κB inflammatory markers by 20-30% in elderly (Houghton et al., Mol Nutr Food Res 2016). Reduced prostate cancer progression biomarkers.

key_papers.title: Pharmacological targeting of the Nrf2-KEAP1 pathway
Sulforaphane and aging: from bench to bedside

dosing.human_dose: 10-60 mg/day (standardized sulforaphane from broccoli seed extract)

safety.known_risks: GRAS. Mild GI (cruciferous compounds). May interact with CYP1A2 substrates (caffeine). Thyroid: high doses may affect iodine uptake.

quantum_sim_params.quantum_advantage_reason: Isothiocyanate-thiol covalent modification involves charge transfer TS — moderate multi-reference character

additional_compounds_genetics_driven.name: Glycine
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.mechanism: Three-fold action: (1) Substrate for glutathione synthesis (glycine + cysteine + glutamate → GSH, rate-limiting in aging); (2) Methyl group homeostasis via GNMT — maintains proper SAM:SAH ratio for DNA methylation fidelity; (3) Anti-inflammatory via glycine-gated chloride channels on macrophages.
additional_compounds_genetics_driven.genetic_basis: Plasma glycine declines 30-40% with age. GNMT expression decreases (epigenetic). The Ornish telomere trial (Lancet Oncology 2013) used comprehensive lifestyle change including glycine-rich diet → telomere LENGTHENING over 5 years.

clinical_evidence.key_result: GlyNAC (glycine + N-acetylcysteine) supplementation reversed 8 of 9 aging hallmarks in elderly humans within 16 weeks (Kumar et al., J Gerontol 2023). Improved mitochondrial function, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored glutathione.

key_papers.title: Supplementing glycine and N-acetylcysteine (GlyNAC) in older adults improves glutathione deficiency, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and multiple aging hallmarks
Glycine and aging: evidence for a role of glycine in longevity

safety.known_risks: Endogenous amino acid. Used in clinical nutrition for decades. No adverse events at 15g/day in trials.

quantum_sim_params.quantum_advantage_reason: No quantum advantage — glycine interactions are classical

refined_pathway_hierarchy.description: From a genetics perspective, the aging pathways are NOT independent. They form a hierarchy. Interventions must respect this hierarchy.

hierarchy.name: FOUNDATIONAL — address before anything else
hierarchy.rationale: These are SUBSTRATE deficiencies. Taurine, glycine, and NAD+ physically decline with age. Without restoring these substrates, downstream interventions (mTOR inhibition, senolysis) are less effective because the cellular machinery lacks fuel.

hierarchy.name: SIGNALING — modulate after substrates restored
hierarchy.rationale: Once mitochondria have fuel (NAD+, taurine) and redox balance (GSH from glycine), THEN inhibiting mTOR and activating Nrf2 can properly upregulate autophagy and suppress NF-κB.

hierarchy.name: CLEANUP — senolysis after signaling optimized
hierarchy.rationale: Clearing senescent cells AFTER restoring cellular health prevents the 'vacuum effect' — where senescent cell removal creates niches that unhealthy (substrate-depleted) cells fill with MORE senescent cells. Mitophagy (Urolithin A) clears damaged mitochondria.

hierarchy.name: MAINTENANCE — telomere/epigenetic (use with extreme caution)
hierarchy.rationale: ONLY after senescent cells cleared and p53/RB checkpoint verified. Telomerase activation in a body full of pre-malignant cells = cancer. AKG epigenetic reprogramming requires intact methylation machinery (which needs glycine/SAM).
safety_gates: Must confirm no active malignancy (PET/CT or liquid biopsy)
Must confirm p53 pathway intact (somatic mutation panel)
Must be AFTER Tier 3 senolysis course
Must be cycled: 3 months on / 1 month off

debate_1_nmn_vs_nr.question: Is NMN or NR superior for NAD+ restoration?
debate_1_nmn_vs_nr.evidence_for_nmn: NMN has Slc12a8 transporter for direct cellular uptake (Grozio et al., Nature Metabolism 2019, DOI: 10.1038/s42255-019-0073-2). Yoshino Science 2021 trial shows human efficacy.
debate_1_nmn_vs_nr.evidence_for_nr: NR must be converted to NMN intracellularly by NRK1/2 but has a transport advantage — enters cells as nucleoside. Martens 2018 shows 60% NAD+ increase.
debate_1_nmn_vs_nr.resolution: USE BOTH in different compartments: NR for hepatic (first-pass conversion), NMN for extrahepatic (direct transporter). OR: just use NMN at 500mg/day — the 2021 Science paper provides the strongest single-compound evidence.
debate_1_nmn_vs_nr.platform_decision: NMN (LNG-001) as primary NAD+ precursor. NR (LNG-002) as backup for NMN non-responders.

debate_2_telomerase_safety.question: Is telomerase activation ever safe in humans?
debate_2_telomerase_safety.evidence_for: Bernardes de Jesus 2012 (EMBO Mol Med): AAV-TERT in 1-year-old mice extended lifespan 24% WITHOUT increased cancer. Key: transient expression, intact p53.
debate_2_telomerase_safety.evidence_against: 90% of human cancers reactivate telomerase. Constitutive TERT overexpression → tumor formation in p53-null mice.
debate_2_telomerase_safety.resolution_from_genetics: Safe IFF: (1) Somatic p53 mutation burden is LOW (liquid biopsy ctDNA panel confirms <0.1% VAF for TP53/RB1/CDKN2A), (2) Dosing is INTERMITTENT (3 months on, 1 off), (3) Preceded by senolytic clearance of pre-malignant senescent cells, (4) Monitored with liquid biopsy every 3 months.
debate_2_telomerase_safety.platform_decision: TA-65 (LNG-008) included with MANDATORY safety gate: ctDNA negative for TP53/RB1/KRAS/CDKN2A

debate_3_rapamycin_immunosuppression.question: Does rapamycin cause dangerous immunosuppression?
debate_3_rapamycin_immunosuppression.evidence_for_concern: Transplant doses (2-5 mg/day continuous): opportunistic infections, impaired wound healing. This gave rapamycin a bad reputation.
debate_3_rapamycin_immunosuppression.evidence_against_concern: Mannick 2014/2018: LOW-DOSE INTERMITTENT (5mg ONCE weekly or even less) ENHANCES immune function — 20% better vaccine response. The dose makes the poison.
debate_3_rapamycin_immunosuppression.resolution_from_genetics: The mTOR pathway is biphasic. High mTOR → suppresses autophagy of intracellular pathogens. Moderate mTOR inhibition → enhances autophagy → BETTER immune surveillance. The key is NEVER achieving transplant-level mTORC2 inhibition.
debate_3_rapamycin_immunosuppression.platform_decision: Rapamycin 5-6mg WEEKLY (not daily). Monitor mTORC1 biomarker (S6K1 phosphorylation) to confirm we're in the 'sweet spot'. Stop if lymphocyte count drops below 1000/μL.

debate_4_senolytic_timing.question: When and how often should senolytics be pulsed?
debate_4_senolytic_timing.evidence: Baker 2016 (Nature): even removing 30% of senescent cells extends healthspan. Hickson 2019: 3-day pulse sufficient. BUT: too frequent clearing → stem cell exhaustion (stem cells share some senescence markers). TOO infrequent → SASP damage accumulates.
debate_4_senolytic_timing.resolution_from_genetics: Optimal: quarterly pulse (every 3 months). Rationale: (1) Senescent cell doubling time in old mice is ~8-12 weeks (Bussian et al., Nature 2018). (2) SASP reaches pathological levels after 2-3 months of accumulation. (3) Stem cells need recovery time between clearance rounds.
debate_4_senolytic_timing.platform_decision: Fisetin 20mg/kg × 2 days, every 12 weeks. D+Q 100mg/1000mg × 3 days only if fisetin insufficient (monitor p16/p21 blood markers).

optimal_longevity_cocktail_v2.description: Evidence-ranked final protocol integrating genetics perspective

tier_2_weekly_signaling.dose: 500 mg/day (or skip if already using rapamycin — see interaction note)
tier_2_weekly_signaling.interaction_note: Rapamycin + Metformin: both inhibit mTOR. Consider alternate weeks if using both. NEVER on same day.

tier_4_conditional_telomere.timing: Only after Tier 3 senolysis + negative ctDNA panel
safety_gates: Age <75 (telomerase less effective after severe telomere loss)

annually: Immune function (vaccine response or lymphocyte subsets)

stopping_criteria: Any ctDNA-positive for oncogenes → stop TA-65, re-evaluate all compounds
eGFR decline > 15 mL/min/year → stop metformin, check other compounds
Persistent GI intolerance → dose reduce or substitute
